_comment: Sourced historical calendar of HIGH-impact scheduled US releases for NEWS-FLAT (NF-P1, docs/plans/2026-10-04-news-flat-preregistration-DRAFT.md): Employment Situation (NFP), Consumer Price Index (CPI), FOMC statements and FOMC Chair press conferences. Every row cites the publisher's own document (bls.gov, federalreserve.gov) or an archive.org capture of the publisher's page; `sources` records each fetched body's sha256 and retrieval time. Nothing is guessed: a time without a source is null with time_status UNKNOWN. Read by scripts/research/news_flat.py (load_calendar).

snapshot.builder: session scratchpad build_calendar.py (fetch log with sha256 per source)

impact_rule: HIGH by release TYPE, fixed before any outcome: NFP, CPI, FOMC statement and FOMC Chair press conference are HIGH in the platform's live calendar policy (docs/architecture/event-calendar.json snapshot v2 scope). The class never depends on the market's reaction. A row without an impact would load as UNKNOWN, never LOW (CLAUDE.md §25).
time_rule: scheduled_event_time is the publisher's scheduled time (UTC; America/New_York converted with the date's own DST state). Windows use it; actual_release_time is never used to move a window (CLAUDE.md §27) and stays null here.
pit_rule: available_time = the earliest evidence that the row's date and time were public (an upper bound: later than the truth is conservative). A row restricts a decision at time t only if available_time <= t and it is not withdrawn by t (withdrawn_available_time <= t). Unscheduled rows never restrict.

statuses.postponed: announced date that did not happen; superseded_by names the new row
statuses.cancelled: announced date that did not happen and was not replaced
statuses.unscheduled: intermeeting FOMC action, never on a calendar in advance (report only)

NFP.basis: every BLS Employment Situation release in the bls.gov archive index from 2004 on; future dates from BLS's schedule page and the latest release (2027 not yet published by BLS)

CPI.basis: every BLS CPI release in the bls.gov archive index from 2004 on; future dates from BLS's schedule page and the latest release

FOMC_PRESS_CONFERENCE.basis: regular press briefings start 2011-04-27 (release of 2011-03-24); none before

unknown.why: no primary source for the release time of the January 2004 - June 2006 statements: the statement pages say 'For immediate release' and the minutes record the release time only from August 2006
no primary source for the 2012 press-conference start times

deviations.what: 2013 lapse in appropriations (BLS: 'suspended from Oct. 1 through Oct. 16')
2018-19: no NFP or CPI release moved (every release from 2018-12 to 2019-02 matched the date and time announced in the previous release of its series)
2025 lapse in appropriations (BLS site notice captured 2025-10-01; revised dates published from 2025-11-14)
2026 lapse in appropriations (BLS site notice captured 2026-02-02; revised dates captured 2026-02-04)
FOMC meeting of 2020-03-17/18 cancelled (replaced by the unscheduled meeting of 2020-03-15)
FOMC meetings extended to two days after their tentative schedule (statement one day later)
documented discrepancies (not deviations of the schedule)
deviations.note: nfp-2012-12-07: the document prints (EDT) on a December date (EST). fomc-stmt-2012-01-25 (and the 2012-04-25, -06-20, -09-13 statements): the press-conference page and the press-release feed show 12:20 / 12:35 p.m.; the minutes record the approved release time 12:30 p.m., which is used.
